AIFS-CRPS: Ensemble forecasting using a model trained with a loss function based on the Continuous Ranked Probability Score
items.meta_description: Abstract page for arXiv paper 2412.15832: AIFS-CRPS: Ensemble forecasting using a model trained with a loss function based on the Continuous Ranked Probability Score
passages: For subseasonal forecasts, AIFS-CRPS outperforms the IFS ensemble before calibration and is competitive with the IFS ensemble when forecasts are evaluated as anomalies to remove the influence of model biases.
For medium-range forecasts AIFS-CRPS outperforms the physics-based Integrated Forecasting System (IFS) ensemble for the majority of variables and lead times.
For the loss, the almost fair CRPS is introduced because it approximately removes the bias in the score due to finite ensemble size yet avoids a degeneracy of the fair CRPS.
Over the last three decades, ensemble forecasts have become an integral part of forecasting the weather.
This paper presents a novel approach to obtain a weather forecast model for ensemble forecasting with machine-learning.
Its loss function is based on a proper score, the Continuous Ranked Probability Score (CRPS).

items.meta_description: ECMWF has taken the Artificial Intelligence Forecasting System (AIFS) into operations today, 25 February 2025, to run side by side with its traditional physics-based Integrated Forecasting System (IFS) to advance numerical weather prediction.
passages: The next steps will be making ensemble forecasts available and introducing experimental data-driven sub-seasonal (extended-range) forecasting.
This is known as ensemble modelling, a technique developed and implemented by ECMWF more than thirty years ago.
